summary: Identity-proxy group cache retains old Okta group ID after group rename, blocking access to InfraRunbook
description:
Issue summary:
Users in the recently renamed Okta group 'infraops-runbooks' are unable to access the internal runbook app 'InfraRunbook' (403). Okta shows correct membership but the Redwood console reports missing RBAC grants tied to the old group ID.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers from two teams cannot access InfraRunbook to follow runbooks during a roll (high operational risk).
- Incident response and runbook edits blocked for affected users until access is restored.

Environment:
- Identity components: identity-proxy v2.3.1 behind ALB in prod/us-west.
- SCIM sync service: scim-sync v1.8.0 scheduled job runs every 5m.
- Okta: group rename performed 2026-03-09 18:32 UTC (group externalId changed).

Steps to reproduce (observed by affected user):
1) User attempts to open https://infrarunbook.internal.redwood.com
2) SAML/Okta SSO succeeds, redirect to app with session cookie.
3) App requests /api/v1/me -> identity-proxy returns 403 with body: {"error":"role_not_found","detail":"no matching RBAC grant for groups: [G-OLD-12345]"}

Observed behavior:
- Okta console shows user is a member of 'infraops-runbooks' (new externalId G-NEW-67890).
- SCIM-sync shows a group mapping entry for G-NEW-67890 -> role infra-runbook-editor.
- identity-proxy logs (snippet) show it continuing to look up G-OLD-12345 from local cache and not resolving to any RBAC entry.

Expected behavior:
- identity-proxy should consider the updated SCIM mapping and grant the role based on G-NEW-67890.

Relevant logs (excerpts):
- identity-proxy (2026-03-10T07:12:21Z): "cache: lookup group:G-OLD-12345 -> hit -> membership: []"
- identity-proxy (2026-03-10T07:12:21Z): "rbac: no grant for groups [G-OLD-12345] user: u_zoe"
- scim-sync (2026-03-09T18:35:02Z): "INFO: created group mapping externalId=G-NEW-67890 name=infraops-runbooks -> role infra-runbook-editor"
- okta (2026-03-09T18:32:15Z): "Group rename: infra-runbooks -> infraops-runbooks externalId G-OLD-12345 -> G-NEW-67890"

Temporary workaround applied:
- On 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC, on-call flushed identity-proxy Redis keys for the 'infra-runbooks' keyspace across three pods (pods id: ip-proxy-12, ip-proxy-13, ip-proxy-14). Access returned for affected users immediately.

Notes on scope:
- This appears specific to group rename events where Okta's externalId changes. Group create/delete flows are handled correctly. The cache invalidation path for group renames is missing.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Jared Bloom | Notified SRE and oncall, collecting logs and affected user list.
2026-03-10 | Priya Nair (oncall) | Flushed identity-proxy cache for affected pods as a stopgap; access restored for 12 users. Will investigate root cause.

2026-03-11 | Ethan Brooks | Reproduced locally by creating synthetic SCIM rename event; identity-proxy continues to serve cached group entries keyed by old externalId. Adding instrumentation to trace SCIM events to cache invalidation.

2026-03-12 | Maria Ortega (SCIM team) | Confirmed scim-sync emitted rename event but payload did not include previous externalId in current implementation; will prepare a scim-sync patch to emit both old and new IDs for rename events.
2026-03-12 | Ethan Brooks | Implemented temporary backfill job to reconcile cache keys by scanning scim mappings and expiring stale keys; deploying canary to prod/us-west.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
1) SCIM sync didn't update role mapping -> disproved: scim-sync shows mapping created.
2) identity-proxy cache TTL too long -> partially true, TTL is 24h and produces long window.
3) Missing cache invalidation path for rename events -> confirmed after reviewing code.

Commands and observations:
- Redis keys pattern: KEYS group:*G-OLD-* => returned keys on prod cluster (ip-proxy-12) showing entries last updated 2026-03-08.
- scim-sync emits event to SNS topic 'scim-events' with type: GROUP_RENAME (payload currently contains new_externalId and name, but not old_externalId).
- identity-proxy subscribes to scim-events but only handles GROUP_CREATE and GROUP_DELETE; GROUP_RENAME handler absent.

Dashboards & links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/d/identity/identity-proxy-cache?orgId=1 (cache-hit-rate spike chart)
- Slack thread: #internal-auth (thread ts: 1689012010.000400)
- SCIM runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ID/pages/SCIM+Event+Spec
resolution:
Partial mitigation: On 2026-03-10, oncall flushed Redis cache keys for affected identity-proxy pods which immediately restored access. On 2026-03-12 a canary of identity-proxy with a backfill job (reconciling scim mappings and expiring stale group keys) was deployed to prod/us-west; canary looks healthy and affected user access remains stable.
Next steps toward full resolution: implement GROUP_RENAME handler in identity-proxy to accept payloads containing old_externalId and expire relevant cache keys on receipt. Coordinate with scim-sync to include old_externalId in rename event payloads.
follow_up_tasks: Add GROUP_RENAME event handler in identity-proxy to invalidate cache keys for old_externalId (owner: identity team; ETA: 2026-03-19)
Patch scim-sync to emit old_externalId in GROUP_RENAME payloads and add integration tests (owner: scim team; ETA: 2026-03-17)
Reduce identity-proxy group cache TTL from 24h to 1h as interim mitigation (owner: infra; ETA: 2026-03-14)
Add alert for sudden mismatch between Okta group externalId and local role mappings (owner: observability; ETA: 2026-03-21)
Audit other services that cache Okta group externalIds for similar rename-handling gaps (owner: security/platform; ETA: 2026-03-24)
Document runbook steps for manual cache flush with safe pod targetting (owner: SRE; ETA: 2026-03-15)
Create postmortem if similar incidents occur during next 30 days (owner: incident commander)
